clues: The dorsal layer of tall columnar cells in the week-2 bilaminar embryonic disc.
It forms the floor of the amniotic cavity and gives rise to amnioblasts.
During gastrulation, cells from this layer migrate through the primitive streak to form all three definitive germ layers.
A narrow midline groove with slightly bulging margins that appears on the caudal dorsal surface of the epiblast at the start of week 3.
It establishes the cranial-caudal, dorsal-ventral, and left-right axes of the embryo.
Epiblast cells invaginate through it during gastrulation to form endoderm and intraembryonic mesoderm.
A flexible midline cellular rod extending beneath the neural tube from the cranial base to the coccyx.
It secretes noggin, chordin, and follistatin to induce the overlying ectoderm to become the neural plate.
In adults, it persists solely as the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral discs.
A transient migratory population of multipotent cells arising along the lateral margins of the neural folds.
They undergo epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition as the neural tube closes.
They differentiate into dorsal root ganglia, sympathetic ganglia, Schwann cells, melanocytes, and the adrenal medulla.
